title: Veridian Contraption by CSL
text: Veridian Contraption by Conflict Simulations LLC View all by Conflict Simulations LLC Creator Follow Conflict Simulations LLC Follow Following Conflict Simulations LLC Following Add To Collection Collection Comments Devlog Related games Related Veridian Contraption A downloadable game for Windows and macOS Buy Now $9.99 USD or more Veridian Contraption Veridian Contraption generates living worlds of procedural strangeness. It runs them continuously. It narrates everything. As of v1.1.0, you don't have to just watch. Step into the world as a living agent, take work, fight, recruit, and if you're lucky, learn magic, while the simulation keeps running around you exactly as it always has. From the Patron's chair you watch a colored map on the left and, on the right, a log written in the voice of a dry bureaucrat. Choose Adventure and you walk in as one person. You start Unknown. In one world, the petition desk at Menvemmond had a bounty on the Thulmtheld Excavation, 52 sp to clear it of its denizens, and the clerk did not look up. Adventure Mode Choose Adventure from the mode screen when a world is ready, or drop into it mid-session from the pause menu, and you become a real living agent inside the same simulation that's been running the whole time. Not a separate mode, not a scripted vignette. The same world, the same economy, the same agents, seen from inside. New in v1.1.1 Pack omens: bump a foe while others stand within reach and the game warns you first. Commit to the Clash, or withdraw before contact. Withdrawing costs time and goes in the chronicle. The death moment: a fallen adventurer gets a full terminal epitaph (cause, tiers, the last lines of their chronicle), and you can read it again from their roster entry. The corruption ceiling: the Art takes any wizard whose corruption reaches its limit. The run ends, but they walk the world still, no longer yours. Arrived in v1.1.0 Adventure Mode: walk between settlements and sites, rest, make camp, and watch the world keep moving while you do. Commissions: take real jobs from settlement petition desks, paid out of the settlement's actual funds, not a fake reward pool. Companions: recruit the people you meet along the way. Friends join free; professionals and citizens want a fee. They fight beside you for real, and retreat to heal instead of vanishing when things go badly. The Clash: turn-based encounters where your decisions decide the outcome, not a die roll. Attack, guard, flee, or cast, if you've learned the Art. Walkable dungeons: descend into ruins and crypts as interiors you explore room by room, not location markers on a map. Magic: real but rare. Study a grimoire if you can find one, or apprentice under a living wizard. Six traditions; power grows with use; corruption is the price, and it never goes away. Retirement and permadeath: retire your adventurer to a roster and they keep living their life in the world without you, or die in battle and let the story end there. Save reliability: v1.0.0 saves load and upgrade automatically; saves write atomically with a 3-deep backup chain that recovers a corrupted file instead of losing your world; crashes leave a log with the world's seed and tick. Combat balance retuned, the encyclopedia and help overlay expanded to cover Adventure Mode, and a long tail of smaller fixes. What it is The gates of Weneld-Uck admitted Ist-Wedilk in the usual manner, which is to say: with neither welcome nor objection. Civilizations rise and decline. Factions schism. Wars start over insults. Harvests succeed. Cults emerge, persecute, escalate, or fizzle. Eschatons arrive. Cosmic indifference asserts itself. The world is doing something on its own, and you are watching it happen. You are spectator, occasional nudge, curator of emergent absurdity. What you get Adventure Mode : embody a living agent inside the running simulation. Travel the world, take real commissions from settlement petition boards, recruit companions with their own lives, fight turn-based encounters ("the Clash"), descend into walkable dungeons, and study one of six magic traditions if you can find a grimoire or a willing teacher. Retire your adventurer to a roster when you're done, or risk permadeath if you're not careful. Nothing here is separate from the simulation. It's the same world, the same agents, the same economy, seen from inside instead of from the Patron's chair. Procedural world generation across five flavor presets and variable sizes 196+ event types across five narrative registers Living agents with goals, relationships, and entanglements Institutional simulation: factions, mergers, schisms, coups, espionage Crafting, equipment, trade, naval trade, ecology, monster lairs Military system with supply logistics, war stakes, political exhaustion, sieges, fortifications, diplomacy Six magic traditions; cults and revolt mechanics R'lyeh Deep One Emergence event; seven Eschaton types Player tools: commissioning, faction founding, look mode, auto-pause alerts In-game encyclopedia (27 sections); log filtering and eleven document report types Original soundtrack with in-game volume controls; sound options at the start menu Byte-identical save/load with 25k-tick determinism guarantee Export functionality; 27-section PDF manual included Soundtrack Fourteen tracks by Ray Weiss. The title ( Movement 2 ) opens the game and is part of the shuffle pool — recurs once per cycle, like any other track, without replacement. ffmpeg-normalized to -16 LUFS. The composition matches the register the simulation has been gesturing at: slow accretion, dense detail, occasional bursts of weirdness, the sense that the world is doing something on its own. Aesthetic lineage Dwarf Fortress · Caves of Qud · The Illuminatus! Trilogy · early D&D modules · Nabokov. Design sources Engels · Dupuy · Clausewitz · Kafka · Principia Discordia · Cohn · Müntzer · Lovecraft · Shea & Wilson. Pricing $9.99 on itch. If you bought in at $3 during Early Access, you're done paying — no upgrade needed for v1.0 or future patches. What's next v1.1 is out: Adventure Mode arrived in v1.1.0, and v1.1.1 is the current build. Veridian Contraption will also debut on Steam down the road, when the storefront is ready. Existing itch buyers get free Steam keys when the Steam debut goes live; no repurchase. If you hit any issues — a crash, a confusing UI moment, a world doing something genuinely weird in a bad way — reach out via the page comments or DM. EA bug reports shaped what shipped; v1.0 isn't the end of the conversation. Status v1.1.1, full release. Windows and macOS. If you've played along through EA, thank you.
